uiContract.shared: One compact app header, current customer/account context, three routes styled as tabs. Use real route links for page navigation; tabs component only for in-page panels. Operator may select a customer; customer identity is always server-scoped. Consistent UTC API instants, SAST display and explicit date boundaries.

flow: Mock sources publish continuously or as a finite reproducible demo scenario
Application consumes events and updates the read model
View categorized transactions and filtered summaries
states: Consumer unavailable; last processed data remains readable
notes: No import jobs, CSV upload or import endpoints.
Totals describe committed processed data; do not label an ongoing stream as completely ingested.
Display asOf and lastProcessedAt with the summary. Consumer lag is diagnostic information, not proof that every external transaction has arrived.
Polling is bounded and paused when the page is hidden; retain a stable query snapshot while paging.
No additional operations dashboard; detailed lag/error metrics remain in observability.

flow: Categorized transaction event is published to Kafka after durable database publication
Fraud consumer applies the event-pinned ruleset
initialRules: HIGH_VALUE_DEBIT: ZAR debit greater than configured threshold
RESTRICTED_MERCHANT: exact normalized merchant in a configured demonstration list
notes: Config/code versioned rules; no DSL or rule-editor UI.
Every completed evaluation saves all rule results, including not applicable.
Temporal velocity rules are deferred; if added, specify late-event and concurrency semantics first.
No review assignment or resolution workflow.

flow: Authorized operator selects account and uploads PDF
Authorized customer/operator issues five-minute bearer link
notes: Show maximum size and PDF-only constraint beside input.
After successful upload clear selected file; retain uploaded document after link errors.
Show absolute expiry and timezone, not a static countdown alone.
Issuing links requires authenticated ownership checks. Possessing a valid link authorizes downloading its document.
No inline PDF preview or access-log dashboard.

modules.accounts: Owns CUSTOMER, ACCOUNT and SOURCE_ACCOUNT and exposes authorized account queries.
modules.transactions: Owns FINANCIAL_TRANSACTION and CATEGORY; normalizes command input, classifies, deduplicates, queries aggregates and publishes categorized events.
modules.ingestion: Spring Kafka listeners and source-specific payload adapters; delegates normalized commands to transactions. Kafka tracks consumer progress; no import job/run/issue tables.
modules.fraud: Owns FRAUD_EVALUATION and RULE_RESULT; subscribes to categorized events and exposes results.
modules.statements: Owns STATEMENT and DOWNLOAD_GRANT; depends only on authorized account API and storage abstraction.
dependencyRules: No cross-module repository access or JPA entity navigation; scalar IDs and public contracts

schemaNotes.core: Five core business tables. CUSTOMER -> ACCOUNT -> SOURCE_ACCOUNT -> FINANCIAL_TRANSACTION, with CATEGORY. No import jobs, source-run leases or import-issue tables. Kafka consumer offsets and dead-letter topics handle stream progress/recovery. Transaction ownership derives through account mapping.
schemaNotes.ids: UUID primary keys for public records; source references remain opaque strings. UUIDs do not replace authorization.
schemaNotes.money: Initial supported currency is ZAR, using NUMERIC(19,2) and BigDecimal created from strings. Reject excessive precision and nonpositive canonical amounts. Store direction separately; support refunds as CREDIT records. Broader currency support requires explicit minor-unit validation, never silent rounding or mixed-currency totals.
schemaNotes.time: Use Instant and TIMESTAMPTZ for events; retain local date-range timezone in query parameters. Use [from,toExclusive). Inject Clock for deterministic expiry and boundary tests.
checks: amount > 0; currency = ZAR initially; direction in DEBIT/CREDIT
Non-null category with seeded UNCATEGORIZED fallback
Fraud outcome must be null unless processing_status is COMPLETED
Statements must be AVAILABLE before issuing or serving a grant
schemaNotes.deduplication: Refines earlier source-only example keys to source-account scoped identities. Same key and identical normalized financial payload is a duplicate; same key and changed payload becomes a conflict for investigation rather than overwriting history. Hash financial/provider content, not categorizer version, so deployments do not create false conflicts.
schemaNotes.crossSourceOverlap: Mock sources intentionally have disjoint provider transaction namespaces. Do not claim cross-provider economic deduplication. Truly overlapping feeds need a reliable shared bank reference or explicit reconciliation policy; matching amount/date is insufficient.
schemaNotes.sourceTruth: Only posted transactions initially; pending-to-posted mutation, double-entry ledger accounting, FX and transfers are out of scope and documented.
schemaNotes.identity: CUSTOMER.auth_subject maps verified authentication identity to customer. Spring Security/session or identity-provider tables are infrastructure and omitted from these ERDs. Operator identity is not a customer ID.
schemaNotes.frameworkTables: Liquibase metadata and Spring Modulith JDBC/JPA event publication tables are infrastructure and omitted from business ERDs. Use the publication registry as the one database-backed externalization mechanism; no second custom outbox or import-progress table.
schemaNotes.deletion: Restrict hard deletes of referenced financial/customer records in this scope; use an explicit retention policy rather than cascading away evidence.
schemaNotes.provenance: Persist first accepted source event ID and original Kafka topic/partition/offset on the financial transaction for diagnostics. They do not replace the provider transaction identity or Kafka's consumer-group offsets.

ingestion: Three separately configured mock producers publish CORE_BANK, CARD_PROCESSOR and WALLET_PROVIDER events to distinct raw topics. Each has stable provider transaction/account references and an independent payload contract.

Use versioned JSON envelopes and checked-in JSON Schemas. Resolve source identity from an allowlisted topic and verify envelope source; authorize source topics with broker ACLs in deployment. Do not trust an arbitrary customerId in the message.
Use record listeners with enable.auto.commit=false and AckMode.RECORD. Listener invokes a separate @Transactional application service; return normally only after the PostgreSQL transaction commits.

Unique (source_account_id, source_transaction_ref) plus normalized financial-payload hash makes retries idempotent. Same key/same content is a no-op; changed content is quarantined as a conflict. Use conflict-aware SQL, not catching a constraint exception inside a rollback-only transaction.

Insert financial transaction, category and Modulith publication atomically; publish only on a new accepted insert. If database commit succeeds but offset commit fails, redelivery finds the existing record and does not create another publication.

Short bounded backoff for transient failures. During a systemic database outage pause/retry the affected consumer rather than rapidly dead-lettering every valid event; offsets do not advance and backlog remains in Kafka.

Invalid schema, unsupported version, unknown account mapping and identity conflicts go to a dead-letter topic with safe error metadata and original source coordinates. Retain unparseable bytes safely where needed; configure deserialization-error recovery.

Configure the recoverer to wait for broker acknowledgement and throw if dead-letter publication fails; advance the original offset only after successful recovery. A crash may duplicate a dead-letter record, so redrive must remain idempotent.
Document a controlled redrive command that republishes to the original topic/key with original business/event identity; do not auto-loop permanent failures.
Bound event size, poll batch size, listener concurrency and database pool use; no detached async processing that returns before persistence.
events: Categorized event publication is persisted by Spring Modulith in the same PostgreSQL transaction as its financial transaction.

Use Modulith Kafka externalization to transactions.categorized.v1, keyed by internal accountId. Mark a publication completed only after the broker acknowledges the send. Configure bounded resubmission, stale publication recovery and completed-entry retention.
No direct dual write of database and Kafka from business code, and no claim that synchronized transaction managers provide a distributed ACID transaction.
Optional fraud consumer uses group fraud-engine-v1, separate from aggregation-v1. Commit its offset after its evaluation/rule-result transaction commits.

Categorized event includes a stable eventId, transactionId, category/version, financial data, occurredAt and the selected rulesetVersion when fraud is enabled. Retry/replay uses that same ruleset; retain executable old rule versions.
Unique (transaction_id, ruleset_version) prevents duplicate evaluations. Persist all results atomically. Missing evaluation is pending or unavailable, never NOT_FLAGGED.

Ordering is per Kafka topic/partition, not global across sources. Asynchronous externalization may reorder categorized publications. Initial per-transaction rules are order-independent; do not add temporal velocity rules without defining late/reordered-event handling.
statements: Write PDF to a generated private staging key with bounded streaming and SHA-256 calculation; never use the original filename as a storage path.
Represent lifecycle as STAGING -> AVAILABLE/FAILED. Finalize storage before AVAILABLE; reconcile stale STAGING rows and orphan files after crashes.
Validate allowed type, size and parseability; MIME header or extension alone is not sufficient. Serve as attachment with nosniff; no inline active PDF content.
Only authenticated authorized operators upload. Malware scanning policy must be explicit before accepting untrusted public uploads.
Use a cryptographically random 256-bit bearer token; persist only SHA-256 token hash. Authorize issuance and validate hash, expiry, revocation and AVAILABLE state at download start.
Expiry prevents starting a new download; it does not revoke bytes already delivered or abort an established stream.
Use Cache-Control: no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, rate-limit issuance/download attempts and redact tokens from logs.
Successful disk write and DB commit are not one ACID transaction; lifecycle/reconciliation handles the gap.

springJava.baseline: One Spring MVC/Modulith application with Spring for Apache Kafka on a supported LTS JDK, compatible GA BOMs, Maven Wrapper, Liquibase and PostgreSQL. Exact versions pinned and compatibility checked during implementation; no snapshot dependencies.
springJava.dataAccess: Spring Data JPA for persistence and DTO projections for reads; use focused SQL for bulk idempotent inserts and aggregates where clearer. Disable Open Session in View and schema auto-update; Hibernate validate only.
springJava.structure: Package by capability with constructor injection. Use records for API/event DTOs, Bean Validation at boundaries, domain checks in services, typed configuration and ProblemDetail error responses. Do not serialize JPA entities.
springJava.transactions: Put short transaction boundaries on application-service calls. No network/file I/O inside long DB transactions. Do not rely on same-bean calls to activate proxy-based @Transactional behavior.
springJava.migrations: Root Liquibase changelog includes module-owned immutable changesets; seed reference categories separately from demo fixtures. Manage framework event tables through migrations, disabling implicit schema creation. Verify both fresh install and prior-schema upgrade.
springJava.auth: Same-origin frontend can use Spring Security sessions with CSRF protection. Local demo credentials/profile are separate from deployment identity configuration. Every query is scoped by authorized account ownership; untrusted customerId is never authorization.
springJava.maintainability: No general workflow engine, custom rules language, generic base-service hierarchy, or microservice split in this scope. Module boundary tests and clear commands/events are sufficient.
springJava.observability: Actuator readiness/liveness, consumer-group lag, processing latency, duplicate and quarantined-event counts, failed publications and structured correlation IDs. Do not put customer IDs into metric labels or tokens/raw financial payloads into logs. Broker/DB incidents do not cause liveness restart loops.

queries: Server-side pagination: default 25, maximum 100; stable non-null (occurred_at,id) keyset ordering.
Bound report date ranges (proposed max 366 days) and event payload sizes; larger exports can be a later asynchronous feature.
Compute SUM/GROUP BY in PostgreSQL; totals cover filtered result set rather than the displayed page.
Use DTO projections and avoid per-row relationship queries; inspect SQL for N+1 behavior.
Use a captured recorded_at cutoff in cursor/report scope for append-only browsing; later reload picks up new rows. Categorization is immutable in this baseline, making the cutoff useful.
Start without aggregate caches; only introduce them if profiling shows a need.
initialIndexes: SOURCE_ACCOUNT(account_id, id) plus unique source mapping
FINANCIAL_TRANSACTION(source_account_id, occurred_at DESC, id DESC) plus unique provider key
FRAUD_EVALUATION(transaction_id, ruleset_version) unique; outcome index only if plans justify it
frontend: Filter/paginate on the server, preserve query parameters in the URL.
Query cache keys include customer/account and every filter; cancel obsolete requests and clear sensitive caches at logout.
Poll transaction summaries only when auto-refresh is enabled and visible; poll fraud results only while pending, with bounded backoff.
Render 25 rows initially; no virtualization or global state store needed.
performance.validation: Publish 100,000 synthetic events across source accounts and measure consumer throughput, lag, duplicate behavior, SQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE, API p50/p95 and heap on documented hardware. This is a benchmark plan, not a result.

acceptance: Fresh clone builds the Java application from source via runnable multi-stage Dockerfile; Docker Compose starts PostgreSQL, Kafka and three independent mock producers with healthchecks and persistent volumes.
Finite deterministic producer scenario yields expected categorized transactions and exact customer/account summaries; continuous mode has configurable rate and stable unique source IDs.
At least two source schemas differ; tests prove normalization rather than relabelling one canonical fixture.
Duplicate delivery, concurrent delivery and crash-after-database-commit-before-offset-commit do not duplicate financial transactions or categorized publications.
Malformed bytes, unsupported schema version, unknown account and conflicting provider IDs are quarantined; failed dead-letter send does not advance the source offset.
Database/broker outages and application restarts recover without silent loss within the documented retention window.
Late-arriving transactions remain queryable by occurredAt; source partitions do not imply global event order.
Exact totals, UNCATEGORIZED fallback, tied-timestamp cursor pagination and no cross-customer access are verified against PostgreSQL.
Categorized event externalization retries after Kafka outage; fraud consumer redelivery creates one result per transaction/ruleset with immutable explanations.
Statement ownership, private storage, expiry boundary, tampered token and interrupted upload behavior pass real API/storage tests.
Testcontainers integration tests use real Kafka and PostgreSQL, with real Liquibase migrations; module verification and API/event-schema contract tests pass.

README identifies Project 1, explains startup, tests, producer scenarios, topic contracts, replay/dead-letter procedure, security assumptions, local single-broker limitations, architecture and optional extensions. Provide the actual GitHub URL.

technicalReferences.topic: Spring Kafka retries and dead-letter recovery

sources.format: integer minor units plus merchant and direction

kafka.producer: Enable idempotent producer and acks=all; retain stable business identities across application-level retries. Producer idempotence alone does not deduplicate arbitrary restarts or external database writes.
kafka.partitions: Proposed 3 partitions per active source/categorized topic; concurrency bounded by assigned partitions and DB capacity. DLT routing preserves source coordinates in headers without requiring matching DLT partition numbers.
kafka.retention: Define finite, configurable raw/categorized/DLT retention and monitor remaining recovery window; Kafka is not indefinite archival storage.
kafka.compose: app + postgres + kafka + bank-source + card-source + wallet-source. Three generators can use one shared Java image with independent source-specific configurations. One local KRaft broker for the submission; production replication, min.insync.replicas, TLS/SASL/ACLs and backup/retention decisions documented separately.
kafka.optionalServices: Monitoring UI may be a Compose profile. NiFi, Flink, Schema Registry and extra application microservices are not required initially.
kafka.localCommands: Planned only: docker compose up --build; ./mvnw verify. No runnable Dockerfile or compose.yaml exists yet.
